title: Sarvam Names Ex-Google Cloud India Chief Sreedharan President and Chief Business Officer
excerpt: Sashikumar Sreedharan, who led Google Cloud India and before that Microsoft India's enterprise business, takes over Sarvam's enterprise and government business and joins its board.
body:
• Indian AI company Sarvam has named Sashikumar Sreedharan, most recently Managing Director for India at Google Cloud, as President and Chief Business Officer. He also joins the company's board.
  • Sreedharan will run Sarvam's business across enterprises and government, and expand its work with digital-native companies, developers and partners. Marketing, finance, forward deployed engineering, service delivery and commercial operations also report to him.
  • He brings more than three decades in technology businesses, including over five years leading Microsoft India's enterprise business and a stint as Google Cloud's Asia-Pacific chief operating officer.
  • Sarvam says more than 100 enterprises and government institutions are now building on its full-stack AI offering.

Sarvam, the Indian artificial intelligence company, has brought in one of the country's most senior enterprise technology executives to run its business, naming Sashikumar Sreedharan — until recently Google Cloud's Managing Director for India — as President and Chief Business Officer.

The company announced the appointment in a blogpost reported by YourStory on Monday. Sreedharan will also join Sarvam's board of directors, and will lead the business across enterprises and government while expanding its work with digital-native companies, developers and partners. Marketing, finance, forward deployed engineering, service delivery and commercial operations will also fall under him.

"India should be a maker of the intelligence the world runs on."

— Sashikumar Sreedharan, President and Chief Business Officer, Sarvam

A career across both US cloud giants

Sreedharan has spent more than three decades in technology businesses. Before Google Cloud, he spent over five years as Managing Director leading Microsoft India's enterprise business — February 2018 to September 2023, according to profiles of his career. At Google, he served as Chief Operating Officer of Google Cloud Asia-Pacific from September 2023 before taking the India managing director role in July 2025, where his work included expanding sovereign cloud capabilities for organisations with strict data-control requirements.

Why Sarvam needs a business chief now

Sarvam, founded in 2023 by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar, builds AI models and applications with a focus on Indian languages and on enterprises owning their AI — data, models and agents staying in-house. The company says more than 100 enterprises and government institutions are now building on its full-stack offering, and it describes its next phase as deepening research, developing products with global appeal and building an organisation that can operate at far greater scale. Industry reports put its funding at $234 million raised in the first close of a planned $300 million Series B round in June 2026, at a post-money valuation of $1.5 billion.

That is the context for the hire: Sarvam's research reputation is established, and the appointment of a career enterprise sales leader — with marketing and commercial operations in his remit, not just partnerships — is the clearest signal yet that the company is organising to sell at scale to India's largest companies and to government.

What to watch

The test of the appointment will be visible in enterprise and government wins over the next two quarters, and in whether Sarvam's developer and partner ecosystem grows beyond its research community. Sreedharan called the move a commitment to the opportunity of India building the intelligence the world runs on; the order book will show whether buyers agree.
